newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom down over five percent.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom down over five percent.

text.p: Shares in newly-floated German telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom fell over five percent on Tuesday, with dealers saying players, including institutional investors, were taking profit.

Telekom shares, which traded for the first time on Monday in Europe's biggest initial public offering, lost 1.80 marks to trade down at 32.10, the lowest level since they started trading, but still well above the issue price of 28.50 marks.
Volumes in the market debutant were strong, with almost ten million shares changing hands in bourse dealings, and over 11 million in computer dealings, where the stock touched a low of 32.05 marks.
Telekom later recovered slightly to trade at 32.20 marks.
"Telekom has been kicked downwards," said one dealer.

Dealers said there had been strong demand on Monday from institutional investors, who had not received as many shares as they would have liked in the heavily oversubscribed flotation. But they said players were now taking profit in the stock.
Investors were divided over whether Telekom would stabilise around current levels or try to climb higher, possibly touching 36 marks.
Meanwhile, the DAX index, in which Telekom is now weighted at 4.5 percent, was down 2.95 points, or 0.11 percent at 2,760.89, fluctuating around its Monday closing level.
